subject: Priv infra: cross-module IaC safety checks + plan verification
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sanjay Patel <s.patel@edgeops.com>
Cc: BrightGrid Technical <infra@brightgrid.com>
Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Priv infra: cross-module IaC safety checks + plan verification

Hi all,

Quick kickoff note for the private-deploy IaC safety work we discussed last week. BrightGrid and EdgeOps expect a tight CI gate for any Terraform/Helm/Ansible changes that touch the on-prem VPC or egress controls. The ask from product and security is: no manual-only rollouts; CI must produce machine-verifiable artifacts we can attach to evidence packages.

Proposed minimums for the gate (we can iterate):
- Terraform: plan parsing step that fails when any change modifies network routing, transit/gateway, or security-group-like rules without an approved RFC id. Output: canonicalized plan JSON and a md5 hash for provenance.
- Helm: values lint + schema check + a diff artifact (helm template vs deployed manifest) included in the pipeline.
- Ansible: idempotence check (run twice in an isolated sandbox) and capture of changed resources produced.
- CI: signed artifact bundle (tfplan json, helm diff, ansible idempotence, pipeline run id) uploaded to a secure GCS bucket (or S3 compatible internal store) and a link added to Jira evidence.

Attachments: priv-iactest-matrix.xlsx (matrix with test types), example-tfvars.yaml (sensitive values redacted).

Next steps: Vanessa/Markus/Irene, can you own a short sprint to scope the pipeline tasks and an example minimal GitLab CI job? Karthik — help surface any runtime constraints for the on-prem airgapped sites. Sanjay — can EdgeOps confirm the storage/location constraints for signed artifacts (internal S3 vs on-prem artifact store)?

I kept the list tight so we can get a working demo by end of week.

Thanks,
Grace

--
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Product Manager, Private Deploy

Date: Sun, 02 May 2027 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Priv infra: cross-module IaC safety checks + plan verification

Thanks Grace — good to align early. A couple of constraints from EdgeOps/ BrightGrid: we operate in an airgapped perimeter for the primary sites. That means:
- No outbound calls to public S3/GCS; artifacts need to land in our internal object store (we'll provide an S3-compatible endpoint).
- Signing must be offline-capable; we use an HSM-backed signing service that can be proxied by the customer's control plane.
- Webhooks to external systems are not allowed; pipeline must write an evidence record (signed meta + link) back to a local Confluence/Jira instance (we will provide URL patterns).

We can accept the plan JSON + md5 approach — we also prefer a short canonicalization step (we use json-stable-stringify) so diffs are stable. I'll attach the artifact acceptance schema on Monday. For now, assume the object store endpoint is: s3://bg-priv-artefacts (internal) and we will provide credentials via an encrypted Vault path.

Sanjay
EdgeOps Integrations

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: draft: pipeline snippets for plan verification

--- snippet start ---
# minimal example (GitLab CI)
stages:
  - validate
  - test
  - package

.tf-plan-guard:
  stage: validate
  image: hashicorp/terraform:1.4.0
  script:
    - terraform init -input=false
    - terraform plan -out=tfplan.binary
    - terraform show -json tfplan.binary > plan-raw.json
    - ./tools/canonicalize_plan.py plan-raw.json > plan-canonical.json
    - md5sum plan-canonical.json > plan-md5.txt
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - plan-canonical.json
      - plan-md5.txt
    expire_in: 7d

.helm-values-lint:
  stage: validate
  image: alpine/helm:3.10.0
  script:
    - helm lint --values values.yaml ./chart || true
    - helm template ./chart --values values.yaml > rendered.yaml
    - git --no-pager diff --no-index --no-color -- rendered-production.yaml rendered.yaml > helm-values-diff.patch || true
  artifacts:
    paths:
      - helm-values-diff.patch

# Ansible idempotence run uses a container with access to a mock inventory
.ansible-idempotence:
  stage: test
  image: docker:20.10
  script:
    - ansible-playbook -i inventory/provision.yml deploy.yml --check | tee run1.txt
    - ansible-playbook -i inventory/provision.yml deploy.yml --check | tee run2.txt
    - diff run1.txt run2.txt > ansible-idempotence-report.txt || true

--- snippet end ---

I'll add lint rules to fail on any plan that adds public_ip, modifies route_table associations, or creates new transit/gateway resources without RFC tag. This should buy the security team traceability they want.

Irene
Infra Reliability Engineer

Subject: Re: Priv infra: cross-module IaC safety checks + plan verification

Thanks for the draft. Two risk items to flag before we bind to implementation: 
1) Egress / NAT changes: many of our on-prem sites share centralized NAT and transit routers managed by site ops. A terraform change that appears local may introduce upstream multicast/bgp impacts. We should require a mandatory network impact field in RFCs (site, owner, downstream IP blocks) and an automated BGP validation (synthetic routecheck) as part of the plan guard.
2) Secrets handling for artifact signing: if we sign artifacts from CI, we must ensure private keys never leave HSM. Our preferred flow is to have CI produce the canonical bundle and request a signing nonce from the HSM proxy; signing happens in the HSM and CI only receives the signature. Looping in security to confirm compliance posture (cc'd).

Also, recommend we add one manual approval step for any change that touches cross-site routing (auto-approval only for tag-only changes). Will create a short RFC template and post to JIRA-OPS-1284.

-Markus
Senior Network Engineer
